body: Almost certainly in the FreeBSD kernel as well. It would be good to document how this is different from BSD-2-clause.

So here is the license text, for convenience:
```
 * Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without
 * modification, are permitted provided that the following conditions
 * are met:
 * 1. Redistributions of source code must retain the above copyright
 *    notice, this list of conditions, and the following disclaimer,
 *    without modification.
 * 2. The name of the author may not be used to endorse or promote products
 *    derived from this software without specific prior written permission.
 *
 * Alternatively, this software may be distributed under the terms of the
 * GNU General Public License ("GPL").
 *
 * THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED BY THE AUTHOR AND CONTRIBUTORS ``AS IS'' AND
 * ANY EXPRESS OR IMPLIED WARRANTIES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE
 * IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE
 * ARE DISCLAIMED. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHOR OR CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE FOR
 * ANY DIRECT, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR CONSEQUENTIAL
 * DAMAGES (INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS
 * OR SERVICES; LOSS OF USE, DATA, OR PROFITS; OR BUSINESS INTERRUPTION)
 * HOWEVER CAUSED AND ON ANY THEORY OF LIABILITY, WHETHER IN CONTRACT, STRICT
 * LIABILITY, OR TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE OR OTHERWISE) ARISING IN ANY WAY
 * OUT OF THE USE OF THIS SOFTWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF
 * SUCH DAMAGE.TWARE, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGE.
```

I now see that the closest match to an existing SPDX identifier is actually another variant with apparent connections to Justin Gibbs, [`BSD-Source-beginning-file`](https://spdx.org/licenses/BSD-Source-beginning-file.html). It basically differs from that one in that `BSD-Source-beginning-file` has ", without modification, immediately at the beginning of the file." The addition of "without modification" is not present at all in `BSD-3-Clause`, `BSD-2-Clause`, or `BSD-Source-Code`, at least as currently formulated by SPDX. Like `BSD-Source-Code` and `BSD-Source-beginning-file`, the traditional clause 2 (covering binary distribution) is omitted. 

I'm not sure how SPDX would deal with the interspersing of the GPL option. I feel that has come up before.

> Almost certainly in the FreeBSD kernel as well. It would be good to document how this is different from BSD-2-clause.

I found it in some files here https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/tree/sys/dev/aic7xxx
such as https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/plain/sys/dev/aic7xxx/aic7xxx_osm.c

This isn't an identical text, but the "CRYPTOGAMS" license (discussed at #2517) is conceptually similar. There are some links in that issue thread to related and prior discussions as well.

I agree that this wouldn't be considered a "match" under the SPDX matching guidelines for `BSD-Source-Code`. I haven't compared against the others that are mentioned above but I'm guessing it's not a match for those as well.

I'm inclined to say that it should probably get its own identifier + entry on the License List.

I don't love the idea of just treating it as an instance of something like e.g. the expression `BSD-Source-Code OR GPL`, for a few reasons:

* The "Alternatively..." text being embedded in the middle of the license probably presents a problem for tooling (or the matching guidelines) that don't expect extra text to appear in the middle of a license.
* If someone who chooses the "BSD-Source-Code" option, it isn't entirely clear to me whether they could choose to omit the "Alternatively..." language altogether. Or, whether that's considered part of the required parts of the license text / notices that they are required to retain. We don't have to answer that here, but the fact that it's a potentially arguable question suggests that a simple `OR` expression doesn't suit here.
* And, the reference to just "GPL" without a version number adds its own complexity.

For similar reasons, I wouldn't suggest adding the "Alternatively..." language as "optional" markup text in the middle of the existing `BSD-Source-Code` license text or others on the list.

Given all of that, my preference is probably to add this as a new license + ID on the License List, with a "notes" section briefly explaining the difference from others on the list. I don't yet have a strong view as to what that name / identifier should be.

**Comment**
We would treat the license as "BSD 3-Clause License (without binary clause)". The alternative provided on a license text level is a reference to a secondary license. This does not contribute to the license identification, but is additional information (on license level) that the license offers options to choose the alternative license, if appropriate.

From our web page:

> **About Secondary Licenses**
The concept of Secondary Licenses is rarely known. Only a few individuals are aware of this concept or its variants. Specifically in the FOSS licensing context, secondary licenses are a defined set of licenses available as alternative for sublicensing an asset, specifically a third-party software component. Secondary licenses may be specifically used to resolve license conflicts when distributing software.
> For the development of a software product, it may be important to understand the mechanics and to have the relevant data available at any time.
> In the {metæffekt} Universe, terms and licenses are modeled on a significant scale. Recently, metadata for secondary licenses has been added, providing detailed information on such options to support informed license conclusions.

See also https://github.com/spdx/license-list-XML/issues/2472#issuecomment-2644039651

For example the EUPL-1.2 offers multiple options as secondary licenses (as 'compatible licenses'):
  - "GNU General Public License 2.0"
  - "GNU General Public License 3.0"
  - "GNU Affero General Public License 3.0"
  - "Open Software License 2.1"
  - "Open Software License 3.0"
  - "Eclipse Public License 1.0"
  - "CeCILL Free Software License Agreement 2.0"
  - "CeCILL Free Software License Agreement 2.1"
  - "Mozilla Public Licence 2.0"
  - "GNU Lesser General Public License 2.1"
  - "GNU Lesser General Public License 3.0"
  - "Creative Commons BY-SA 3.0"
  - "European Union Public License 1.1"
  - "LiLiQ R License 1.1"
  - "LiLiQ R+ License 1.1"

```
[...]
Compatibility clause: If the Licensee Distributes or Communicates Derivative
Works or copies thereof based upon both the Work and another work licensed under
a Compatible Licence, this Distribution or Communication can be done under the
terms of this Compatible Licence. For the sake of this clause, ‘Compatible
Licence’ refers to the licences listed in the appendix attached to this Licence.
Should the Licensee's obligations under the Compatible Licence conflict with
his/her obligations under this Licence, the obligations of the Compatible
Licence shall prevail.
[...]

‘Compatible Licences’ according to Article 5 EUPL are:

  works other than software

- Québec Free and Open-Source Licence — Reciprocity (LiLiQ-R) or Strong

```

**Comment*
+1 to add as specific license. Proposing the name following the "BSD 3-Clause License (without binary clause)" idea.

This license is much closer to BSD-Source-Code than to BSD-3-Clause.  I feel like the name 'BSD-3-Clause (with some extra stuff)' is more confusing than 'BSD-Source-Code (with some extra stuff)'.

As for dealing with the 'Alternatively' clause, the legal wording clearly makes this an 'OR', whether tooling can handle the parsing or not.  If the 'Alternately' clause were to appear after the disclaimer text, if would not present a tooling problem, and this would be a straightforward 'BSD-Source-Code OR GPL-2.0'  (ignoring the slight text differences between this version of BSD-Source-Code and the canonical one at: https://spdx.org/licenses/BSD-Source-Code.html

There are other instances of license statements in the Linux kernel that are much thornier than this.  I don't think this one
really needs a secondary compatible license statement.

I'm happy to change all instances of the clause ordering in the Linux kernel source code, if that will help with tooling.

As for the 'naked' GPL (that is, GPL without a version number), my policy for the Linux kernel is to treat all un-numbered GPL references for code submitted after September 1992 as GPL-2.0.  This is when the COPYING file was introduced as the kernel license file; and all ambiguous contributions, IMHO, after that date can safely be assumed to be under that version of the license.

> As for the 'naked' GPL (that is, GPL without a version number), my policy for the Linux kernel is to treat all un-numbered GPL references for code submitted after September 1992 as GPL-2.0. This is when the COPYING file was introduced as the kernel license file; and all ambiguous contributions, IMHO, after that date can safely be assumed to be under that version of the license.

A license scanner must evaluate this from the given context. Sometimes this is impossible as the information when the code was first added is not easily accessible or not at all available.

> This license is much closer to BSD-Source-Code than to BSD-3-Clause. I feel like the name 'BSD-3-Clause (with some extra stuff)' is more confusing than 'BSD-Source-Code (with some extra stuff)'.

Nevertheless, you are omitting the 2nd clause (3rd clause in the default BSD 3-Clause template). For the universe we have a defined policy handling this and this policy applies to not just one instance of a BSD variant. Our naming approach **values commonalities over specifics**, which I regard as good generally applicable choice.

> As for dealing with the 'Alternatively' clause, the legal wording clearly makes this an 'OR', whether tooling can handle the parsing or not. If the 'Alternately' clause were to appear after the disclaimer text, if would not present a tooling problem, and this would be a straightforward 'BSD-Source-Code OR GPL-2.0' (ignoring the slight text differences between this version of BSD-Source-Code and the canonical one at: https://spdx.org/licenses/BSD-Source-Code.html

For me the differences are
1) is the statement part of the license text (as an intrinsic part of the text) --> secondary license
2) is the statement not part of the license text, but an additional hint on a licensing option --> or GPL
BTW. I regard the identification of ScanCode as GPL-1.0+ as imprecise. I always wonder, why this doesn't cause further discussion as an obviously false statement.

This is when the COPYING file was introduced as the kernel license file; and all ambiguous contributions, IMHO, after that date can safely be assumed to be under that version of the license.

If the source code has an SPDX-License-Identifier line, then the license scanner is trivial.  I am not doing automated license scanning to determine the identifier to assign -  I'm going file by file through the kernel and examing relevant data (author, date of submission, possible origin outside the kernel, etc.) for each one.  For the kernel, I have a record of every commit and every patch contribution since the kernel's inception.

I am of the very strong opinion that the statement is not part of the license text (option 2).
+1 to add as a new license based on historical precedent of doing this with other licenses that have the "Alternatively" clause in the middle of them (e.g., Brian-Gladman-3-Clause)

Are you'all seriously going to treat the "Alternately ..." language as if it is part of the license text?

@tbird20d - well, it is part of the license text, at least in how it's drafted. We have come across this before, it's super annoying, and spent a bunch of time wrangling with this in light of the goal of SPDX being machine- and human-readable. As to the former and for matching licenses, that involves the ability of license scanners to match to text. When someone moves paragraphs around or inserts something like this in the midst of the license text, it's really hard to maintain the match-ability-ness. 

I'm probably not explaining that well (b/c it's annoying!), but here we are.  @swinslow may have a more eloquent way to describe this.
